description:
FOUND s499j (pre-existing: identical on the base 61571685/937e7b65).  `pcl -e 'die "x"'` prints on stderr

    While evaluating the form starting at line 24, column 0
      of #P"/tmp/pcl_NNN_XXXX.lisp":x at -e line 1.

where perl prints `x at -e line 1.` (exit 255 on both).  The same program run as a FILE (`pcl f.pl`, the script-cache path) prints the one perl line.  CAUSE (suspected, not measured): the transpile-to-a-temp-file path loads the .lisp with plain CL `load` (pcl's quiet_load_form), whose error reporting wraps the condition with the form position; the script-cache path goes through the runtime's own loader.  CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: run the same temp .lisp through `p-load-with-recovery` / the script-cache loader and compare stderr.  USER rule (s494): errors must fail in the same places as perl and be TIDY -- one line, never a Lisp wrapper.  Paths: `pcl -e`, `pcl -E`, `pcl -M Mod script.pl`, `pcl --no-cache script.pl`.

=== MEASURED s506f (Opus, s507 resume, 2026-10-04) — the cheap discriminating measurement, TAKEN ===
The SAME temp .lisp of `pcl -e 'die "bye\n"'` (and of `print "a\n"; BEGIN { print "B\n" } die "x"`) run two
ways (scratch/s506f/s507/f2measure.pl + f2measure.log in worktree agent-a908d9d2d9fff4ce2):
  (1) pcl's quiet_load_form (SOURCE load)             -> "While evaluating the form starting at line 24 … :bye"
  (2) the script cache's loader: %p-build-module-fasl, then %p-load-module-fasl (fallback %p-load-script-text)
                                                       -> "bye"   (perl's one line; status 255 both)
So the suspected cause is CONFIRMED: the source load prints the context, the fasl load does not (#1595).
A prototype in `pcl` (program_load_form: seed *p-core-inc-dirs* + *pcl-pl2cl-path* as script_cache_form does,
build the fasl beside the temp .lisp, open it, delete both, load the stream; text fallback) made 11 of 12
probe shapes byte-identical to perl (scratch/s506f/s507/f2.sh; the 12th = a STDIN program's die exits 9 under
perl — die's status is $!, EBADF left by perl's own read of the program) at +2 % on a 1,000-line --no-cache run
(3.336 s -> 3.409 s median of 3) and ~0 on a one-liner.
NOT SHIPPED — what killed it: the fasl BUILD runs `(p-eval-always (p-require-file "./x.pl"))` at COMPILE time
with *standard-output* bound to a broadcast stream, so a require'd file's top-level output is LOST and at load
%INC says it already ran — exactly #2686, which today bites only the FIRST (cache-building) run of a script; on
the -e path EVERY run is a first run.  Measured: Pl/t/pcl-switches-01.t's row "a require'd file's #! line is
NOT examined" (`-e 'require "./req1.pl"; print "after\n"'`) printed only "after".  So #2492 is BLOCKED BY #2686:
fix #2686 (the build must not run a require'd FILE's body, or must replay its output), then the program_load_form
above is the whole #2492 fix.  Also NOT covered even then: a compile-time `use` that fails makes the BUILD fail,
and the text fallback prints the context again (`pcl -c -e 'use NoSuch;'`, `pcl FILE.pl` with a missing module).
subject: An uncaught die under `pcl -e` (and `pcl -M … script`) prints SBCL's "While evaluating the form starting at line N, column 0 of #P\"/tmp/pcl_….lisp\":" before perl's message -- two lines where perl prints one (the script-cache path does not)
